title: Green card started
ask: Do you know the date your PERM was filed with the Department of Labor? Add it in Me as your priority date.
why: The PERM filing date becomes your priority date, the one number that decides how long you wait. Ask HR or counsel for it and keep a copy of the ETA-9089.

title: I-140 approved
ask: Does the I-140 approval notice show the priority date and category (EB-2 or EB-3) you expected, and do you have your own copy?
why: Errors on the notice are easier to fix early, and you will need the copy for every future extension and to carry the date to a new employer.

title: This month's Visa Bulletin
ask: Have you checked this month's bulletin for your category, and which chart USCIS is accepting (Dates for Filing or Final Action Dates)?
why: If your priority date is before the Dates for Filing cut-off and USCIS accepts that chart, you can file the I-485 with a work permit and advance parole now, even though approval is years away.

links.label: Which chart to use this month (USCIS)

title: Waiting for your priority date
ask: Are your I-485 documents ready for the month your date becomes current: birth certificates (with a non-availability certificate if needed), marriage certificate, photos, full I-94 and I-797 history, employer letter, and a plan for the civil-surgeon medical (I-693)?
why: Filing in the first month a date is current matters because dates retrogress. Indian birth certificates and medical appointments are the usual delays.

title: Waiting for your priority date
ask: When EB-3 India moves ahead of EB-2, have you discussed with your employer or counsel whether a new EB-3 I-140 (keeping your EB-2 priority date) makes sense?
why: A downgrade lets you file the I-485 under whichever category is current. It is a strategy decision with costs and timing risks, not a form you file alone.

title: I-485 pending
ask: Biometrics done, and have you received your EAD and advance parole (combo card)? Add the card's expiry date in Me.
why: The card is your fallback if H-1B or H-4 status ever breaks, and its renewal should be filed about 180 days before it expires.

title: EAD expires within 6 months
ask: Have you filed the EAD (and advance parole) renewal?
why: USCIS accepts renewals up to 180 days early. Automatic extensions for pending renewals were removed for applications filed on or after 30 October 2025, so a late filing can mean a gap in work authorisation.

title: Travelling with a pending I-485
ask: Will you re-enter with a valid advance parole document, or with a valid H-1B or H-4 visa stamp? Never leave with neither.
why: Leaving the US with a pending I-485 and no advance parole abandons the application, unless you hold and re-enter in valid H-1B or H-4 status.
